correctness.rationale: Every concentric bicentric tetrahedron has an orthogonal-box parametrization. Its facet-normal centers form a dual disphenoid of circumsphere radius L>1. The four face triples of unit balls meet uniquely at contacts p_i of length rho: acuteness gives positive barycentric weights, and weighted squared-distance averaging forces the singleton intersection. Fourfold intersection is excluded below L by the centroid squared-distance identity. The Čech complex therefore has only the stated 6 edge, 4 triangle and 1 tetrahedron entry scales, and their canonical boundary matrices give the full barcode and integral nonbounding at the threshold. The original 2-cycle cannot die under any central radius q<rho because no 3-simplex is present; at q>=rho every proper outer subset meets the central ball, giving a cone. Inverse coordinate formulas exactly reconstruct the original tetrahedron. The packaged script checks 208 nondegenerate examples but is not used to infer universal truth.

value.rationale: The exact origin-centered radius rho required to fill the genuine bounded void gives a previously unstated topological characterization of the central ball in the five-ball construction. The complete all-scale 0/1/2-dimensional Čech classification of its four outer generators is natural in union-of-balls geometry and, unusually, its birth thresholds determine the entire disphenoid congruence class and the cavity-filling radius. This is a complete motivated geometric family classification with an inverse theorem, not merely a numerical recomputation or a cosmetic deduction.
